limitations: Transport faults are deliberate instrumentation around real PostgreSQL, not observations of spontaneous network loss in production.
A lost COMMIT acknowledgement does not prove rollback. Four tests execute COMMIT first, then raise a synthetic acknowledgement error; the committed state is retained and the client reports failure.

Typed replay APIs enforce payload.context against the trusted caller scope. The inherited low-level privileged SQL function was read and remains unchanged; direct privileged SQL payload semantics are a separate trust boundary.

Original atomicity coverage includes a first test whose direct app-pool read is blocked by RLS and checks the committed event separately; the new InTx test provides an explicit profile/event rollback pair.
All customers, approvals and actions are synthetic. No physical action or independent human decision is demonstrated by these tests.
